title: Preference pair builder: screening, margins, standings
scenario: Screen labelers on a calibration round, convert position-relative 1-7 ratings into margins in favour of model A, aggregate per pair into A/B/tie verdicts, export chosen/rejected training pairs and rank models by win rate with an alphabetical tie-break.

verified.why_correct: The two branches look reversed, but a low rating means the left response won, so 4 - rating is positive exactly when the left (model_a) response is preferred; when model_b was on the left the sign flips.
`abs(margin) < 0.5` matches the spec: only values strictly inside the band are ties, so P06's 0.5 is decided for A.

bugs.title: Calibration judgements not deduplicated
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_labeler_quality: lab-09 shows checks 5, accuracy 0.6, excluded True (expected 4 / 0.75 / False). All verdicts are unchanged, because lab-09 judged no regular pairs.
bugs.why: Only the regular judgements go through latest_only. lab-09 re-did calibration pair C2, so both the wrong first attempt and the corrected one are counted, 3/5 = 0.6, and lab-09 is excluded.
hints: lab-09 has 5 checks, but there are only 4 calibration pairs. How?
Compare how the two judgement files are prepared in build_report.
Wrap the calibration load in latest_only(...) as for judgements.csv.
probes: Why does excluding lab-09 change none of the verdicts?
Which of lab-09's two C2 submissions should count, and why?

bugs.title: left_model compared without normalising
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_pair_margins: P08's margin is 0.67 instead of 1.33. Every other margin matches, and P08's verdict is still A.
bugs.why: Pair models are lower-cased at load, but left_model is only trimmed. j022 has `Cobalt-70b` on the left, so the comparison fails, the judgement is read as if model_b was on the left, and its +1 margin becomes -1.
hints: Only P08's margin is off. Recompute its three judgements by hand.
Look at how margin_of decides which model was on the left.
probes: Why does P08's verdict still come out as A?
Why is calibration unaffected by the same function?

bugs.title: reverse=True also reverses the name tie-break
bugs.new: return sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (r["win_rate"], r["model"]), reverse=True)
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_standings: cobalt-70b (0.75) is listed before atlas-7b (0.75); birch-13b and delta-3b are in the right places.
bugs.why: reverse=True flips the whole key tuple, so equal win rates come out in reverse alphabetical order. atlas-7b and cobalt-70b are both 0.75 and swap places.
hints: The numbers are all right. Which two rows are out of order, and what do they share?
Look at the sort in standings.
Negate win_rate in the key and drop reverse=True.
probes: Why doesn't reverse=True work for a mixed descending/ascending sort?
How else could you sort descending by one field and ascending by another?

context_qa.a: It loads the labeler registry (id -> active flag), the pairs, and both judgement files, screens labelers with `quality.labeler_quality` on the calibration judgements, keeps the non-excluded labelers, aggregates the regular judgements with `aggregate.aggregate`, and builds the dataset and standings from those results.

context_qa.q: How does latest_only pick a judgement?
context_qa.a: It keys on `(pair_id, labeler_id)` and replaces the stored judgement whenever the new one's `submitted_at` is `>=` the stored one, so the latest wins and, on equal times, the later row. Output order is first-seen key order.
It decides whether model_a was on the left by comparing the judgement's `left_model` against `pair.model_a`, then returns `a_margin(rating, left_is_a)`.

context_qa.q: How is left_model stored by the loader?
context_qa.a: `load_judgements` stores it with `clean()`, i.e. trimmed but with its original case. Pair model names go through `norm_model` in `load_pairs`.

context_qa.q: Which labelers appear in the quality table?
context_qa.a: Every labeler whose active flag is true, sorted by id. `checks` is how many calibration judgements were counted for them in `labeler_quality`; accuracy is None when that is 0.

context_qa.q: How does standings count a tie?
context_qa.a: Both models get one entry in `ties`. Win rate is `(wins + 0.5 * ties) / games` rounded to 3 decimals; pairs with verdict `insufficient` are skipped.
